what_it_does: This paper develops a digital twin—a computational simulation—that processes real-time underwater sensor data to predict tsunami waves from earthquakes in the Cascadia Subduction Zone (off the Pacific Northwest coast). Offshore sensors detect acoustic pressure changes created by seafloor motion during an earthquake; the system solves complex 3D physics equations (coupling acoustic and gravity waves) with one billion unknowns to infer what actually happened on the seafloor, then forecasts wave propagation to enable coastal warnings. Traditional Bayesian inference of such large systems was computationally impossible; this work makes it feasible using novel parallel algorithms and runs inference on 43,520 GPUs.
